title: Demolishing the Edwards Plateau for a Golf Course b/w Spiritual Colon Cleanse for a Diseased Society
source_creator: Joey Santore / Crime Pays But Botany Doesn't
primary_use: Edwards Plateau limestone flora, local species recognition, milkweed pollination, and Asteraceae phyllary-based identification

rights.public_reuse: not assumed cleared; obtain separate permission/license before publication

curation_rules: Prefer source-explicit on-screen labels over noisy auto-captions for taxon spelling.
Keep source interpretations attributed when ecology or behavior is inferred rather than directly visible.
Do not promote source names/range claims to canonical taxonomy without the normal project reconciliation step.
Retain genus-level uncertainty when Joey/source overlay does not resolve species.
notes: Very high-value local Edwards Plateau source with multiple on-screen labels and repeated demonstrations of thin-soiled limestone habitat.
Matelea reticulata sequence is especially strong for whole-flower orientation, hairy corolla/sepals, reticulate venation, nectar, and milkweed-family floral complexity.

Asclepias asperula sequence clearly shows a honeybee on the flowers and supports Joey's pollinia/hood discussion; the exact effectiveness of other insect visitors should not be inferred from still frames alone.
Tetragonotheca texana sequence is a strong generic Asteraceae lesson because Joey explicitly uses the phyllaries to distinguish a yellow composite.
Castilleja lindheimeri hemiparasitism is source-derived context; retain as Joey's field explanation until authoritative promotion.
Galium remains genus-level in the source and should not be forced to species.
